title: Regional admission controller telemetry & SLI hydration dashboard
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Add fine-grained telemetry and a Grafana dashboard that shows how the regional admission controller (hotspot-aware admission + per-shard queueing) affects token-level and request-level SLIs across regions, and surface circuit-breaker hysteresis states for smoother failover decisions.

Scope:
- Instrument admission decisions with tags: region, shard, model_variant, reason (capacity|latency|kv-prefetch|burst).
- Emit per-request derived metrics: admitted_tokens, dropped_tokens, admission_latency_ms, queue_time_ms, admission_decision (allow|defer|reject).
- Correlate admission events with token-latency SLI windows (p50/p95/p99 per model_variant and region) and KV cache hit rates.
- Build a single-pane dashboard with: regional admission rate trends, admitted vs dropped token heatmap, admission_latency distribution, circuit-breaker state timeline, and SLI hydration panel that shows how many SLI samples were produced per region and how sampling bias changes during a failover.
- Add alert rules: sustained drop_rate > 1% for 15m (severity: P1) and circuit-breaker flapping > 3 toggles in 10m (severity: P0).
- Document runbook steps for admission-related incidents and include a canary rollback procedure for admission policy changes.

Why this is important: during recent multi-region incidents we lacked visibility into whether increased tail latency was due to aggressive admission policy, KV cache churn, or kernel scheduling hotspots. This work will give ops a direct signal to decide between relaxing admission thresholds, provisioning burst capacity, or triggering regional failover.

Trade-offs/notes:
- We will sample request traces at 1% by default to avoid high-cardinality costs; however admission counters must remain un-sampled.
- Adding tags increases metric cardinality; we will roll out model_variant and shard tags in stages and evaluate cost after 1 week.
- Correlating cache hit-rate requires aligning EKF timestamps; a short smoothing window (30s) will be used to avoid misattribution.

Rollout plan:
1) Backend metrics & minimal dashboard (staging)
2) Load-test with synthetic traffic harness (ENG-48888) to validate cardinality and SLO sample counts
3) Deploy to canary region for 48h with traffic mirroring
4) Full multi-region release + runbook distribution to SRE/Oncall

Success criteria:
- SLI hydration panel shows >=95% expected SLI samples within 1 hour of deployment for top-5 models.
- Alerts trigger correctly during a simulated admission surge in the harness.
- Oncall can use dashboard to attribute a real incident to admission policy vs kernel hotspots in < 25 minutes.

2025-02-27 - Jun: Implemented deny/retry/requeue reasons and added admission_latency_ms histogram. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1486 (waiting review).

2025-03-03 - Load test results: synthetic burst 3x baseline for 30m. Admission dropped_tokens rose to 2.3% at p99, KV hit-rate dropped 8% concurrently. This indicates admission policy interacting with cache churn. Added follow-up task to tune cache prefetch TTL.
